headline: Enterprise AI is shifting to Agentic Workflows, moving past passive chatbots
summary: Most enterprise AI initiatives fail due to passive chatbots. The next evolution is agentic, where AI executes tasks autonomously, providing real operational leverage.
details: Most enterprise AI initiatives fail because companies bolt chat interfaces onto databases, which business users don't want. They need data to execute work, not just chat about it.

The 'ChatGPT wrapper' era is peaking. The next evolution in enterprise software is agentic, not just generative. Passive conversational agents create human bottlenecks, as users still interpret answers and execute tasks manually.

An Agentic AI system equips a large language model with tools, memory, and agency, allowing it to generate actions instead of just text. It performs tasks on behalf of humans, eliminating manual intervention.
This approach functions as dynamic, self-healing Robotic Process Automation (RPA), overcoming the brittleness of traditional RPA. Agentic systems adapt to changes that would crash older scripts.
Consider a supply chain exception: a delayed shipment. An Agentic AI system can asynchronously update the ERP, check production schedules, and notify sales, all without human data entry.
Building Agentic AI is 80 percent traditional software engineering and 20 percent AI. Success depends heavily on robust internal data infrastructure, not just clever prompts.

Reliable agents require strict typing, clean API endpoints, robust error handling, and solid DevOps pipelines. This involves managing API rate limits, authentication, and hallucination guardrails, essentially building distributed microservices orchestrated by an LLM.

Companies that will dominate the next decade will possess the most autonomous backend workflows, not merely the smartest internal chatbots. This shift drastically reduces operational overhead by building systems that execute.

headline_marked: [[Browser becomes a compute platform]] with Edge AI, WebGPU, and WebAssembly
headline: Browser becomes a compute platform with Edge AI, WebGPU, and WebAssembly
summary: Modern web applications now run complex workloads locally, leveraging client CPUs and GPUs. This shift offers faster, cheaper, and more private real-time experiences by reducing reliance on backend infrastructure.
details: Browsers are evolving from simple presentation layers to high-performance execution environments. This enables complex workloads previously impossible, leveraging CPU cores, GPU accelerators, and shared memory for near-native performance.

This architectural shift is driven by Edge AI (client-side compute), WebAssembly (WASM), and WebGPU. These technologies fundamentally change how engineers design scalable applications, moving compute closer to the user.

Traditional web models faced bottlenecks with increasingly compute-intensive tasks, leading to rising GPU inference bills and accumulated latency. Transmitting information to cloud infrastructure also introduced compliance, security, and privacy concerns.

WebAssembly allows compute-intensive workloads to execute inside dedicated Web Workers, preventing main thread blocking. It compiles code into a compact binary format, achieving approximately 90-95% of native performance while maintaining browser portability.

WebGPU addresses GPU limitations, providing a next-generation graphics and compute API designed around modern hardware standards. For the first time, browser applications can leverage GPU hardware similarly to native desktop applications, dramatically accelerating browser-based AI.

Edge AI enables machine learning models to execute entirely within browser environments, often with surprisingly small memory footprints. Instead of calling cloud APIs, applications can increasingly perform inference locally, reducing backend compute costs.

One significant performance killer in browser compute workloads is memory copying; modern architectures increasingly rely on SharedArrayBuffer to eliminate unnecessary duplication. This pattern allows JavaScript, Web Workers, and WebAssembly modules to operate on the same memory region without serialization costs, yielding substantial gains for large-scale pipelines.

This architectural evolution is driven by practical benefits, not just new technology. Every inference executed locally is one less executed on cloud GPUs, allowing many AI-powered products to dramatically reduce backend compute costs and improve real-time performance.
caption:
The browser is no longer just a UI. It's becoming a high-performance compute platform, running AI models and complex visuals locally.
